cases.name: game-refusal
cases.why: SpaceTraders refused the action in this ship state. The gateway relays the game's status, body and content-type unchanged (st-gateway/src/server.ts, the `res.status(upstream.status)` relay).

cases.name: game-cooldown
cases.why: A 409 from the game, and a different remedy from a refusal: wait, rather than change what you asked for. Only the status and the sentence say which.

expect.message: Ship action is still on cooldown.

cases.name: game-token-rejected
cases.why: SpaceTraders rejected the agent token the gateway injects — not the caller's own session, which every service verifies before the gateway is reached. The gateway has already refreshed the credential and retried; a 401 arriving here means that did not help, so an operator has to look at auth-service.

gateway.body: {"error":{"message":"Token reset_date does not match the server. Expected: 2026-09-06, Actual: 2026-08-16","code":401}}

cases.name: rate-limited
cases.why: A 429 the gateway could not absorb, passed through with its pacing headers. The gateway forwards retry-after and the x-ratelimit-* trio precisely so a caller can pace itself; relaying the status without them keeps the news and drops the instructions.

expect.message: You have reached your API limit.

cases.name: credential-not-configured
cases.why: auth-service has no agent token yet. An operator has to act; nothing retries its way out of it. This exact sentence is the only signal that says so — the gateway's other 503 means the opposite.

cases.name: auth-service-unavailable
cases.why: The same status as the case above, and a problem that resolves on its own. Relaying the message is the whole of what keeps them apart.

gateway.body: {"error":{"message":"auth-service unavailable: cannot obtain a SpaceTraders credential"}}

expect.message: auth-service unavailable: cannot obtain a SpaceTraders credential

cases.name: spacetraders-unreachable
cases.why: The gateway exhausted its retries against the game. It is a 502 because the gateway decided so — the client did not, and could not have.

cases.name: gateway-proxy-failed
cases.why: The gateway's own handler threw, or an upstream body died mid-read. Also a 502, and also the gateway's verdict rather than the client's.

cases.name: body-too-large
cases.why: The gateway's own 5 MB body limit. A 413 relayed as a 413 tells the caller to send less; relayed as a 502 it tells them to try again, which will not help.

cases.name: non-envelope-error-body
cases.why: A proxy or load balancer between the client and the gateway answering with HTML. There is no message to lift, so the raw body stands in, truncated.

cases.name: oversized-error-body
cases.why: The truncation cap, which had drifted to 64 KiB in one service and 500 characters in another. An error message is read by a person; echoing a megabyte of someone else's HTML through three logs is not diagnosis.

cases.name: empty-error-body
cases.why: A non-2xx with nothing in it at all. Still relayed by status; the message is the client's own, because there is none to relay.

cases.name: gateway-unreachable
cases.why: No response at all: connection refused, DNS failure, read timeout, or a body that died mid-read on the client's side. The one condition the client itself gets to classify, because the gateway never spoke.

cases.name: unusable-success-body
cases.why: A 2xx the client cannot parse at all. The gateway answered and the client cannot pass it on, which is what 502 means here.
